extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians specializing in arithmetic geometry and Mochizuki's Inter‑Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and formulates the structural requirements, constructions, and compatibility conditions appearing in Corollaries/Remarks/Definitions concerning F-prime-strips, F_l-symmetries, localization/realiﬁcation, Kummer isomorphisms, and related Frobenioid data in IUTch II. Targeted at formalizing the conditions and compatibilities one must satisfy when building these objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial construction of F-prime-strips (per label j)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each label j ∈ LabCusp(†D), there is a functorial algorithm in the category †D for constructing an F-prime-strip F(†D)|j from F(†D) which is well-defined up to isomorphism (cf. [IUTchI], Example 5.4, (iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction is to be regarded as canonical up to isomorphism and is the basic labeled-local object attached to a label j; it is used as input to produce localization functors, symmetrizing isomorphisms, and diagonal constructions. See Corollary 4.7(ii) and related references.

rubrics_metrics.name: F_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms between labeled data
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural poly-action of F_l on †D induces isomorphisms (called F_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms) between the labeled data attached to distinct labels j ∈ LabCusp(†D) (e.g., between F(†D)|j, M_mod(†D)j, {πκ-sol ...}j, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These isomorphisms are compatible (relative to the bijection †ζ) with the F_l-symmetry of associated bridges (D-NF-bridge / NF-bridge). They are subject to prescribed conjugacy indeterminacies (see next criterion) and determine diagonal subobjects as formal shorthand. See Corollary 4.7(ii) and Corollary 4.8(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugacy indeterminacies for objects with πrat/κ-sol/∞κ subscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects equipped with subscripts/superscripts such as “mod”, “sol”, “κ-sol”, or “∞κ” (or ‘πrat/κ-sol’) are only defined up to certain conjugacy indeterminacies; for distinct labels j these act independently, together with a single conjugacy indeterminacy that is independent of j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of introducing these subscripts is to synchronize certain conjugacy actions so that diagonal constructions can be formed without contending with independent unsynchronizable indeterminacies. See Remark 4.7.2 and the discussions in Corollaries 4.7 and 4.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonal F-prime-strips / diagonal sub-pseudo-monoids / diagonal subcategories (formal shorthand)
rubrics_metrics.description: One may form diagonal collections (e.g., diagonal F-prime-strips, diagonal sub-pseudo-monoids, diagonal subrings, diagonal subcategories) as a purely formal notational shorthand for the collections of labeled objects tied together by the F_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a formal device (not an additional geometric object) used to denote the collection invariant/linked by the symmetrizing isomorphisms; conventions about what “(−)j” denotes follow Corollary 4.7(ii) and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization functors and reified global structures (per label j)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each j there is a functorial algorithm producing 1-compatible collections of localization functors / poly-morphisms (up to isomorphism) mapping the global/module/Frobenioid objects indexed by j to their localized or realiﬁed counterparts (including realification denoted by superscript R), together with natural isomorphisms of Frobenioids and of topological monoids at each v ∈ V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These localization constructions must be compatible with the bijections involving 'Prime(−)', with the local isomorphisms of topological monoids, and with the F_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms. They are constructed functorially in the relevant categories (cf. Corollary 4.7(iii), Corollary 4.8(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer isomorphisms of pseudo-monoids (non-realiﬁed global structures)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm in the relevant Frobenioid categories for constructing Kummer isomorphisms of pseudo-monoids (the first two of which carry group actions and are well-defined up to a single conjugacy indeterminacy); these give rise to 'Kummer-theoretic' isomorphisms between π1-type objects, and compatible isomorphisms of Frobenioids (including mod and realified versions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Kummer isomorphisms are the mechanism producing compatible identifications between various πκ-sol / M∞κ / M_mod objects and underlie the Frobenioid isomorphisms used in gluing and localization (see Corollary 4.8(i)). The group-actions and single-conjugacy-indeterminacy proviso must be tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of all constructions with F_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms and NF-bridge symmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: All isomorphisms, localization functors, Kummer isomorphisms, realiﬁcations, and diagonal constructions are required to be compatible with the F_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms (and with associated NF-bridge / D-NF-bridge symmetries) and with the bijections (e.g., †ζ) that index labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility is repeatedly asserted as a necessary condition (e.g., Corollary 4.7, Corollary 4.8, multiple Remarks). When constructing or checking maps, one must verify that they commute with these symmetrizing actions and indexing bijections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction: non-realiﬁed global Frobenioids only in the presence of F2_l-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-realiﬁed global Frobenioids (e.g., 'Fmod' as a global object) only make sense to consider in the context of the F2_l-symmetry, because considering them anabelian/Galois‑theoretically requires the full profinite group ΠCF and the subgroups ΠCK, ΠXK are only defined up to ΠCF-conjugacy; the resulting indeterminacies involve F2_l-poly-actions and cannot be quotiented away without 'label-crushing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes a structural constraint: do not attempt to form non-realiﬁed global Frobenioids except under F2_l-symmetry, and be aware that quotienting by the indeterminacy is not legitimate as it destroys the essential labeling used in Gaussian monoid constructions (see Remark 4.7.6 and subsequent discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: F3±-symmetry vs F2_l-symmetry (additive vs multiplicative dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: F3±-symmetry corresponds to the additive combinatorial dimension (think: units, includes zero label 0 ∈ |Fl|) and is suited to conjugate synchronization and coricity (uniradial aspects). F2_l-symmetry corresponds to the multiplicative combinatorial dimension (think: value groups, excludes zero label) and is suited to separating zero from nonzero labels and to multiradial formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use F3± for constructions concerning local units, conjugate synchronization, and coric uniformity; use F2_l for constructions concerning Gaussian monoid internal structure, multiradiality, and separating coric constant distributions from nonzero components (see Remarks 4.7.3–4.7.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: do not symmetrize zero and nonzero labels under F2_l
rubrics_metrics.description: Symmetrizing zero and nonzero labels in the context of the F2_l-symmetry (i.e., treating them as if '0 ≪ 0') would be incompatible with weighted volume computations and thus is an absurd operation; the zero label parametrizes coric common data and nonzero labels parametrize components subordinate to zero with weight assignments (volumes at j assigned weight 1/l) that preclude such symmetrization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When handling Gaussian monoids and weighted volume computations, preserve the separation of zero and nonzero labels under F2_l; avoid any constructions that collapse this distinction (see Remark 4.7.3(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial/étale-picture modeling of symmetries (spokes and gluing at 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model the uniradiality (F3±) and multiradiality (F2_l) combinatorially via an étale-picture: copies of Fl (or |Fl|) indexed by spokes (each spoke = an arithmetic holomorphic structure) glued at the coric label 0; on each spoke there is a corresponding action of the relevant F-symmetry, with F3±-actions on distinct spokes failing to commute and F2_l-actions on distinct spokes commuting and compatible with spoke permutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combinatorial visualization guides intuition about commutativity and synchronization properties; use the étale-picture illustrations (Fig. 4.1, 4.2) and the rules about commuting actions when reasoning about multi-spoke constructions (see Remark 4.7.4(i)–(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of radial environments and radial functor (uniradial vs multiradial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form radial environments by taking coric data objects 0_α (zero label subscripted by spoke α) and radial data copies (Fl)_α or |Fl|_α; define arrow-sets between spokes based on the existence of combined actions, and define a natural radial functor from radial data to coric data; the resulting environment is uniradial for F3± and multiradial for F2_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a concrete combinatorial formalization of symmetries suitable for producing uniradial/multiradial radial environments; the construction should follow the arrow/existence rules described in Remark 4.7.4(iii) and is analogous to the switching functor/parallel transport remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical interpretation & subordination structure (addition atop multiplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two symmetries reflect a hierarchical two-dimensional combinatorial structure (addition and multiplication) analogous to units vs value groups or two cohomological/real dimensions; this hierarchy manifests as a subordination relation '≪' used in computation of weighted volumes and is reflected in which conjugation actions (geometric fundamental group vs absolute Galois) give rise to the respective symmetries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting constructions, keep in mind which symmetry corresponds to which cohomological/geometric source (F3± from geometric fundamental group; F2_l from absolute Galois group) and how the hierarchy affects allowable identifications and volume computations (see Remark 4.7.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realified localization and eventual use of units via log (Gaussian monoid realification policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Realiﬁed localization functors concern only the realification of the Frobenioid-theoretic version of Gaussian monoids; the unit portion will later be used additively (via the 'log' operation) rather than multiplicatively in subsequent work (IUTchIII), and non-realiﬁed global Frobenioids function as translation apparatus between multiplicative and additive (log-shifted) line-bundle notions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement realification only where indicated and maintain natural splittings of Gaussian monoids required for log-shifts; ensure localization functors/morphisms are constructed to permit later log-based additive interpretations (see Remark 4.8.1–4.8.3 and Remark 4.8.2(i),(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperate vs profinite conjugates theory linkage and resolution of conjugacy indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory of 'tempered versus profinite conjugates' (IUTchI, §2) is applied to resolve certain profinite conjugacy indeterminacies that appear in local portions of Hodge theaters and is linked via gluing operations to the profinite indeterminacies in other Hodge theaters; this theory provides a method to understand/resolve such indeterminacies in proofs (e.g., Corollary 2.4(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confronting profinite conjugacy indeterminacies in gluing/localization arguments, apply the tempered vs profinite conjugates framework as in IUTchI §2 and the indicated Remarks/Corollaries to control or resolve these indeterminacies (see Remark 4.7.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: ×-Kummer and ×μ-Kummer structures on a Frobenioid C
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Frobenioid C with base category D and universal covering pro-object A (G = Aut(A)), a ×-Kummer structure (resp. ×μ-Kummer structure) on C is defined to be a Z×- (resp. Ism-) orbit of isomorphisms κ×: O×(G) ∼→ O×(A) (resp. κ×μ: O×μ(G) ∼→ O×μ(A)), where O×(A), O×μ(A), μN(A) etc. are the monoids/groups obtained by evaluating O(−) at A and carry natural G-actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a precise structural definition (Definition 4.9) specifying the data and symmetry/orbit conditions that constitute a Kummer structure; when specifying such a structure one must identify the universal cover A, its automorphism group G, and the relevant torsion/units quotients, and then produce the isomorphism or its orbit under the indicated group.
